title: kbroot.without_paths keeps an unquoted absolute path with a space when a newline follows it, since ABS_PATH_BARE has no re.M
goal: kbroot.without_paths removes an unquoted absolute path that holds a space whole when text follows it on the next line, so a multi-line exception text keeps no fragment of the path. Found by the SP-c6tr77jl review (S3, kbroot.py ABS_PATH_BARE, BG-ngtix6e2).

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kbroot;o=kbroot.without_paths("cannot create /home/jan.kowalski/my cache\nsecond line");print(repr(o));sys.exit(1 if "/home" in o or "my cache" in o else 0)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbroot
o=kbroot.without_paths('cannot create /home/jan.kowalski/my cache\nsecond line')
e=kbroot.without_paths('cannot create /home/jan.kowalski/my cache')
print(repr(o),repr(e));sys.exit(0 if 'second line' in o and '/home' not in o and 'my cache' not in o and '/home' not in e and 'my cache' not in e else 1)
